A per-coordinate shift (sigma^{k_1}P_1,...,sigma^{k_m}P_m) with unequal k_i is not in that group and is not addressed by A1/A2 or by the census. Mathematically it is also not a symmetry in general: on G, sum lambda^{k_i}P_i = R only if sum (lambda^{k_i} - 1)P_i = 0, which fails generically for any m (except through the global shift, which changes R). (2) MEASURED, toy tier, m=2 only: BIN-TOY-K19 (n=19, V={deg<10}, non-stable, 50 targets, 85 certified decompositions): same_instance_hits=0, conjugate_hits=1.0, leg-swap 1.0, shifted legs in V 0.0. The unsound-canonical-constraint demonstration lost only 11 solutions, with a median lost fraction of 0.0, outside the pre-registered band; the quantitative 1-1/n prediction MISSED and only the qualitative claim (lost > 0) held. The strength 'replicated' means arm and seed replication of one implementation: no independent validator (PD-1), manifests dirty-at-write. The same_instance_hits=0 result is nearly tautological at the non-stable K19 cell, because shifted legs leave V (in-V 0.0). The experiments therefore confirm a proved lemma on toys; they carry no independent evidential weight about m>2, n=131 or auxiliary-variable encodings. Stage 0 also computed ord_n(2) (131: 130; 163: 162) and marked ECC2K-130 and K-163 STRUCTURALLY_EMPTY for stable V, which is arithmetic and not m-dependent.
argument_depends_on_m: The argument for C1 does not depend on m. (a) Lemma A1: sigma is a ring endomorphism and S_{m+1} has coefficients in F_2 for a,b in F_2, for every m. (b) Lemma A2: the disjointness reduces to x(sigma R) != x(R) (x(R)^2 != x(R), i.e. x(R) not in F_2), which for R in G\{O} holds because sigma acts on G as a scalar lambda with lambda^2+lambda+2 = 0 mod r (a=0). lambda = +-1 would need r | 2 or r | 4, so sigma R != +-R. No m enters, so the x-only sign ambiguity (2^m sign patterns) does not rescue it. (c) Auxiliary intermediate-point encodings (chains X_j = P_1+...+P_j with S_3 constraints, Petit-Quisquater / Huang-Kosters-Yeo style). Applying sigma uniformly to every variable, endpoints and intermediates, is the same equivariance, and the chain for x_R maps to the chain for x_R^2. Applying DIFFERENT powers sigma^{a}, sigma^{b}, sigma^{c} to X_{j-1}, X_j, P_j is not a symmetry. It would need (lambda^a-lambda^b)X_{j-1} + (lambda^c-lambda^b)P_j = 0 as an identity, which holds only if a=b=c (lambda has order n=131, prime, and the points have pseudo-random discrete logs mod r). On a particular solution it is a new coincidence of probability about 1/r, not a structure. Hence m, chaining and auxiliary variables do not change C1. (d) What does vary with m (my own derivation, NOT in the ledger): the group Z/n wr S_m (per-slot Frobenius shifts with slot permutations). An element (pi, k_1..k_m) with some k nonzero fixes a tuple only if, on each pi-cycle of length c, x = x^{2^{kc}}. For n=131 prime and m<131 that forces kc = 0 mod 131 (impossible for c<131) or x in F_2, i.e. an E(F_2) point and never a DLP target. So for m up to ~20 and up to 130 the sigma-part acts freely on tuples. Only at m >= n=131 do cycles of length n appear, giving sigma-fixed tuples (x_i = x_1^{2^i}) that sum to a Frobenius trace in E(F_2). That is irrelevant for m ~ 20. (e) Group computation: the point-level symmetry of one fixed-target instance is S_m. (Z/2)^m negations act trivially on x-tuples but change the point sum, which is why the x-only system is the sign-disjunction. The algebraically available bijections of x-space (translation by the unique nontrivial point of E[2](F_2-bar) = T=(0,1) giving iota: x -> sqrt(b)/x, equal to 1/x for b=1, which I verified from the chord formula; plus the semilinear Frobenius powers; Aut_O(E) = {+-1} since j=1/b != 0) are generated by iota and sigma. A signed-shift-permutation element g = (pi, eps_i, k_i, t_i) changes the point sum by sum_i (eps_i lambda^{k_i} - 1) P_{pi(i)} + (sum t_i) T. For this to vanish on the whole affine hyperplane sum a_i = log R it needs eps_i lambda^{k_i} = 1 for every i, forcing k_i=0 and eps_i=+. The only extra stabilizer is therefore iota on an EVEN number of legs, order 2^{m-1}, which grows with m and commutes with sigma. It exists only if V is iota-stable. A linear subspace V is iota-stable only if it is a coset of a subfield (b^{1/4}F_{2^d}), empty at prime n=131 (cofactor-torsion lead). A non-subspace iota-stable V is not excluded by C1; it belongs to the nonlinear-frob-stable-bases and cofactor leads. Any element sigma^k * (iota^t, slot permutation) with k != 0 maps R to lambda^k R != +-R, so it fixes no instance. A union-of-shifts base B = U_k sigma^k V is sigma-stable as a set, but sigma still maps (R,B) to (sigma R, B): equivariance again. Because the action is free, the solution set of the orbit system modulo sigma equals the solution set of one target, so the orbit-system search is the single-instance search. This supports the free-quotient reading behind C3 and C4 without needing m. (f) m enters only in the toy statistics (the 1-1/n lost fraction, what fraction of shifted legs lands in V), not in the lemma.

A cost-neutrality ratio of 1.00-1.47 at m=2 could therefore hide a factor of order m! at larger m, because the baseline counts conflicts per separately solved system. (4) Mixed-shift products lose the geometric structure of the (A,P) linear oracle. For geometric V = theta<1,g,..,g^{l-1}>, span(sigma^aV . sigma^bV) has exponents 2^a(i+2^d j) with d=|a-b|, so dimension is at most about (2^d+1)l for small d and approaches l^2 for large d, versus 2l-1 for d=0. And A = X_2+X_3 lies in a 2l-dimensional sum instead of V. This is my own derivation, unverified, but it matches the repo's own caveat (geometric_v_linear README line ~119). It implies the oracle reach depends on the shift differences, hence on the pattern class and on m. (5) Per-slot Frobenius shifts are not symmetries of one fixed-target instance at any m, because they change the base, not the target. A genuine argument (same as Lemma A1 and Prop Sigma) supports that part of the closure for every m. Sporadic halving coincidences (Lemma A2-prime) are not a group action, also for every m.

The cited H-CERTBIN-adccf3 / EXP-CERTBIN-a14350 was never run (runs/ holds only .gitkeep; the idea is status 'proposed', novelty 'unverified'). Proposition T is stated for a single F_2-subspace V. H-CERTBIN-adccf3 line 266 explicitly puts orbit-union bases out of scope. C4 contains no statement, proof or experiment about U_k sigma^k V with per-slot shifts. Restrict to patterns with small pairwise shift differences d. For geometric V, span(sigma^aV . sigma^bV) has dimension at most (2^d+1)l, so a restricted-pattern union keeps a linear (A,P)-style oracle while multiplying the base by about the number of allowed shifts. This gives an intermediate between the pure pattern (fraction n^{-(m-1)}) and the full union. It is my derivation and is unverified. Equivariant elimination on a union base: the revisit_when trigger 'an equivariant elimination that applies to the production compact-orbit pipeline' is not excluded by C4. In the pattern decomposition, system(sigma^j R, k) and system(R, k-j) are the same system, so elimination work could be shared across patterns of one target, which Proposition T's T4 only denies for a fixed non-stable V.

overall_assessment:
Verdict: the closure is sound where it is a proof, overscoped, and miscited in places. It is not wrong, and it does not rest on m = 2 or 3 where it is a proof. The owner's belief that only small m was examined is correct for the experiments but mostly not for the arguments.

What is proved, for every m:
- C1 (the absolute Frobenius is an equivariance between conjugate targets, not a symmetry of one instance) rests on Lemma A1: S_{m+1} has F_2 coefficients, so coordinatewise squaring maps the ideal I_R to I_{sigma R}. This holds for every m and for chained encodings, provided sigma is applied uniformly to every variable.
- Independent per-slot or per-intermediate Frobenius shifts are not a symmetry of a fixed-target instance at any m. They would need sum (lambda^{k_i} - 1) P_i = 0, which holds with probability about 1/r.
- The same-instance stabiliser comes out as S_m, plus the even-weight 2-torsion translations (order 2^{m-1}) when V is iota-stable. This stabiliser calculation is the audit's own derivation, not a ledger theorem.
- Proposition T is also a two-line identity valid for all m. It says that on a non-stable V the n conjugates of a target are n attempts over n conjugate bases.

What is only measured, and only at m = 2 or 3:
- C1 and C2 experiments: m = 2 only, n = 17 or 19.
  - They are close to tautological censuses of the lemma, with no CNF or SAT solver.
  - Strength "replicated" means seeds of one implementation.
  - The quantitative loss-fraction prediction for the canonical-constraint test missed its band; only the qualitative sign held.
- C3 is unsupported as worded.
  - The ">= 0.95x at n = 17, 23, 31" figure is a pre-registered falsification threshold from H-BINSTD-c72284, which is still "approved". Only Stages 0-1 ran: no solver, outcome O-RELABEL-READY, Stage-2 SAT census not authorized.
  - The real data are in KN-FIND-47da4e: m = 2, n = 13, 17, 19, 23, orbit-union of a random non-stable V, unverified/preliminary. Conflict ratios 1.017, 1.017, 1.467 and 1.150 against the SUM of n gauge-fixed systems, not a plain single-instance search.
  - n = 31 and linear stable V were never run for cost.
  - m = 3 is named there as the "natural next cell" and was never built.
  - The baseline n^{m-1} overcounts distinct systems by a factor tending to m!. The exact class count is D(n,m) = C(n+m-1,m)/n, so the m = 2 result could hide a factor of order m! at larger m.
- C4: the m-independent identity is proved. The second half ("k conjugates of a relation are one row in the orbit basis") is hand-proved but has never been run.
  - H-CERTBIN-adccf3 has zero runs (EXP-CERTBIN-a14350 contains only .gitkeep).
  - H-BINSTD-ce4f38 Part 2 is blocked.
  - Proposition T covers a single subspace V. Union bases and per-slot shifts are explicitly out of scope there.
  - On a sigma-stable union base the n conjugates are ONE attempt, so "n attempts" does not apply.
- C5: all equivariant numbers are m = 2 with l = 3 fixed and n <= 13 (64-bit monomial limit).
  - The 15.5x oracle ratio rests on 3 decomposing targets, and 11.6x of it is non-equivariant fall-row augmentation (F/C is only 1.25-1.34).
  - The "regresses 0.29-0.59x on production" figure is NOT a measurement of the equivariant pass. It is arm F (plain fall-row augmentation) at m = 3, in a non-production layout. The production-order re-measure gives 0.64-0.91.
  - The equivariant pass was never run on any production system. "Does not apply" is structural, not measured.
  - 44-73x versus 2-3x is a naive-versus-crate-kernel baseline correction. It is real, but not evidence of "constant only": the control ratio vs gf2_elim grows 0.82, 2.15, 3.15 for n = 7, 11, 13 and is unmeasured at n >= 17.

Where the owner's belief is wrong:
- The group does not usefully grow with m for Frobenius. Per-coordinate shifts are not symmetries at any m.
- For prime n = 131 and m < 131, the sigma-part acts freely on tuples.
- The groups that do grow are S_m and (Z/2)^{m-1} (2-torsion). They are not Frobenius.
  - S_m lex symmetry breaking was tried at m <= 3, n <= 15 and gave no help (conflicts 5512 vs 6412 at m = 3, n = 9).
  - The 2-torsion symmetrisation is implemented only to m = 3. The XP-20261018 card (m = 4) is blocked and unbuilt.
- Faugere-Svartz needs an abelian group of order prime to 2, so only the odd part of S_m is usable (C_3 at m = 3, 4).

Where the owner is right:
- All SAT/CNF evidence for orbit encodings is m = 2.
- The sound orbit encodings have never been built or measured at m >= 3.
- Large-m infrastructure exists but was never used for orbit-vs-plain ablations.
  - The m = 4..6 chained-S3 SAT with Frobenius orbit domain at n = 83 was only built; K = 2048, m = 5 stopped at 1,000 conflicts, UNKNOWN. The "ordered" arm there is S_2, not Frobenius.
  - The m = 10 rotated-slot circuit exists with no committed solve result.
- The lead's wording ("forecloses ... all m", "n = 17, 23, 31 >= 0.95x") is stronger than the evidence.

Recommended lead edits: downgrade C3 from proof to "measured at m = 2, unverified; m >= 3 untested"; split C5 into the measured equivariant result (m = 2) and the separate arm-F regression; add the non-stable and union-base qualifier to C4.

ideas.title: Common-shift symmetric production system: parity bound for the equivariant quotient and the m*(n,D) crossover
ideas.mechanism: Re-gauge instead of union. On a non-stable V (prime n, so V is never sigma-stable except F_2 or the whole field), the n conjugate attempts system(R, sigma^k V) are the n attempts of Proposition T. The first idea builds the ONE sigma-symmetric system that contains all n of them over the production chained-S3 shape. Variables are the chain intermediates X_1..X_{m-2} (n coordinates each), the slot coordinates c_i in F_2^l (fixed by sigma), a shared shift selector s (one-hot, n), a target selector s0 (one-hot, n) and aux u_i = sigma^k x_i(c_i) (n each). Then N_p = ml + (m-2)n for one attempt and N_s = ml + 2mn for the symmetric system. This is smaller than the m=2 barrel (5n+2l) because one shared s replaces per-slot selectors. Group C_n acts on s, s0, X, u by cyclic shift and fixes c. For D < n only monomials containing no cyclic variable are fixed by a nontrivial element (a fixed monomial must contain a whole n-block), so by Burnside the number of orbit columns is (C(N_s,<=D) - C(ml,<=D))/n + C(ml,<=D). Key structural point: if refutation uses selector-linear certificates 1 = sum_k s_k * cert_k, the Macaulay space splits along the one-hot selectors into n^2 component matrices (k,j) that C_n permutes in n free orbits. The quotient then stores n distinct component matrices, which is exactly n separate attempts, so the equivariant quotient has cost parity (gain <= 1/pi, with pi the per-entry penalty of F_{2^d} versus F_2 arithmetic). The quotient can beat n attempts only if the unrestricted joint space refutes at the SAME degree as one component (D_u = D_c). If D_u = D_c + 1, parity is the best case. This is the m-dependent version of the step-gate failure already seen at m=2 (symmetric system cubic, gauge-fixed quadratic: C has one linear consequence fewer, research/ic_improve_20261014/02-equivariant-oracle/README.md section 4).
ideas.exact_claim: (i, derived and Lean-able) For D < n and the common-shift symmetric system above, the orbit-column count is (C(N_s,<=D) - C(ml,<=D))/n + C(ml,<=D), and a selector-linear certificate space has quotient dimension exactly n * C(N_p,<=D_c), i.e. parity with n separate attempts. (ii, measured) On the toy cells (m,n,l) in {(3,5,1),(3,7,1),(3,7,2),(4,5,1)} the XL/Macaulay refutation degree D_u of the symmetric system equals D_c + 1, where D_c is the maximum over the n conjugate attempts of their XL refutation degrees measured by the same instrument. If instead D_u = D_c in any cell, the model G = n^2 * C(N_p,<=D_c) / C(N_s,<=D_c) applies and the equivariant quotient wins above a crossover m*(n,D). Derived m*: about 4 for D=4, about 7 for D=5 at n=131 (l from the yield rule), and none at m=2 or 3.

ideas.title: Group-ring (F2[X]/(X^n-1)) monomial-pivot elimination: fold first, DFT only when forced
ideas.mechanism: The measured equivariant pass diagonalises at once: it forms dense character blocks over F_{2^d} (research/ic_next10_20261014/06-equivariant-f4-m4/README.md section 3; RESEARCH_G2_EQUIVARIANT_F4_SCOPE.md section 3.1). Dense blocks cost the sparsity of the Macaulay rows. At step level the crate's sparse-friendly gf2_elim beats the dense blocks until n about 15: I/C = 0.40x, 0.70x, 0.97x, 1.05x, 1.65x, 1.63x at n = 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23 (research/ic_improve_20261014/02-equivariant-oracle/README.md section 4). The idea is to eliminate in the group ring R_n = F2[X]/(X^n-1) BEFORE the Fourier transform. The folded matrix has (rows/n) x (cols/n) entries, each a polynomial sum_t P[r, sigma^t c] X^t that is mostly 0 or a single monomial, because each unfolded row has exactly one image per orbit column. A monomial X^t is a unit with free inverse X^{-t}, and for n=131 R_131 = F2 x F_{2^130} so a polynomial is a unit iff its weight is odd and it is not J = 1+X+...+X^130. A row operation row_i += X^t * row_p costs about 3 word XORs plus a rotation per entry (131 bits = 3 words), versus about n unfolded entries; it is the exact folded image of n^2... unfolded F2 row operations. Pivot greedily on monomial (or odd-weight non-J) entries, Markowitz order, until no cheap pivot remains or mean entry weight exceeds a threshold, then project the remainder to the trivial block (X->1, F2) and character blocks (X->zeta, F_{2^d}) as now. Rank identity is preserved because unit pivots are units in both components.
ideas.exact_claim: On the symmetric barrel Macaulay matrices already generated by the repo (m=2, l=3, degree 3, n = 11, 13, 17, 19, 23), a Markowitz monomial-pivot R_n elimination with a density-triggered switch to the existing character blocks yields (a) identical rank and degree-fall row space (rank identity 13,595 / 20,999 / 43,019 / 58,259 / 98,759 reproduced), and (b) at least 2.0x lower CPU than the current dense-block arm C at n = 19 and 23, with the number of pivots performed before the switch >= 30% of the rank. Predicted interval for the C/new ratio at n = 23: [1, 8]; central guess 3x (a guess, stated as such).

Folding only has a payoff where the symmetric matrix is a joint (non-block-diagonal) space; it cannot compress genuinely different component matrices (see idea 1), so the m-dependence is carried by how coupled the joint space is, which this idea measures through fill-in.
ideas.math: Unfolded sizes (measured): n=23 symmetric 120,379 x 273,262, orbit blocks 5,297 x 11,880 over F_{2^11} (two blocks chi1, chi5, each orbit of 11) plus trivial block rank 4,335; n=19: 71,677 x 158,558 -> 3,835 x 8,344. Entry model: nnz(folded) = nnz(unfolded)/n; initial entry weight is at most the number of t with P[r,sigma^t c] = 1, expected about 1 on nonzero entries because each unfolded entry maps to one orbit column. Units: for prime n with ord_n(2) = n-1 (n=11, 13, 19, and 131), R_n = F2 x F_{2^{n-1}}; non-units are exactly even-weight elements and J. For n=17 (R = F2 x F_{256}^2) and n=23 (F2 x F_{2048}^2) the unit criterion is odd weight and nonzero in each component. Cost accounting: monomial pivot row operation = q entries * (3 word XOR + 1 rotate) at n=131, replacing n^2 F2 row operations on rows of length n*q; the dense phase after the switch has block dimension reduced by the number of pivots already done. At n=131 a full-density entry operation is a 3x3-word carry-less product (9 PCLMUL) plus a cyclic wrap, so the dense phase is not worse than the F_{2^130} block arithmetic assumed already. Worked toy: n=7, d=3, R_7 = F2 x F_8 x F_8; with a monomial pivot X^3 the row op multiplies by X^4 (inverse of X^3 mod X^7-1), a rotation of a 7-bit word.
ideas.why_closure_does_not_apply: C5 says equivariant elimination is 'a constant only: 44-73x vs a naive kernel is 2-3x vs gf2_elim'. That statement measures one design (DFT up front, dense blocks, table arithmetic at d <= 18) against the crate kernel; it says nothing about folded sparse elimination. The same README shows step-level I/C growing 0.4x -> 1.65x with n, so the dense-block design is still improving against the sparse kernel, and the measured loss at small n is attributable to density, which this idea targets. The lead's revisit_when ('an equivariant elimination that applies to the production compact-orbit pipeline') is not met by idea 2 alone: it is the elimination half, and it needs the symmetric system of idea 1 for production shapes. The closure also records F/C = 1.25-1.34 as the only equivariant gain on the oracle, so idea 2 is judged at step level, not by oracle tree collapse.

ideas.title: Shared-prefix echelon reuse across targets and conjugates: equivariance used only to re-gauge
ideas.mechanism: Proposition T lets the n conjugate attempts system(R, sigma^k V) be rewritten as system(sigma^{-k} R, V): the same base V for every attempt, with sigma applied to the target. In the chained-S3 production system the first m-2 equations S3(x1,x2,X1)=0, S3(X1,x3,X2)=0, ... do not contain R at all; only the last equation S3(X_{m-2},x_m,R)=0 does, and src/cryptanalysis/polynomial_reuse.rs already records that the final link is D + sum_k r_k C_k (target bits r_k enter linearly over fixed polynomials). So for FIXED V every target (and every conjugate) shares the Macaulay rows generated by the first m-2 equations. Reduce those rows to echelon once per (n, m, l, V), store it, and per target reduce only the rows generated by the target-dependent equation against the stored echelon. This is not an equivariant quotient and needs no symmetric system, but it is the production-applicable form of the saving that equivariance was meant to give across conjugates, and its benefit grows with m, which is the owner's question. InheritedF4 (src/cryptanalysis/ic_framework/solvers.rs HybridKind::InheritedF4) inherits a reduced basis from parent to child inside one split tree; it does not reuse across targets, and polynomial_reuse.rs stores polynomials, not reduced rows (no 'echelon' or 'rref' match in that file).
ideas.exact_claim: For the chained-S3 production system with V = span(1,...,z^{l-1}), the degree-D Macaulay pass for a target costs, with the shared-prefix echelon precomputed, a fraction about 1/(m-1) of the full re-elimination in the dense F2 model, so the per-target gain is at most m-1 (2x at m=3, 3x at m=4, 7x at m=8, 19x at m=20), independent of n and l; at m=2 (no shared equations) the gain is exactly 1.0. Measured claim: on n = 11, 13, 15 with m = 3 and 4 and l about n/m, the incremental pass returns the identical row space and refutation bit as the full pass (exact), and its CPU ratio full/incremental lies in [1.2, m-1] with the m=2 control within 3% of 1.
ideas.m_regime: m = 2 (negative control, exact 1.0), 3, 4, 5, 6 at toy n (known matrices from examples/ic_next10_06_chain_export.rs, e.g. (n,l)=(9,3),(13,4) at m=3; (6,2),(9,3),(11,4) at m=4); m = 8..20 by counting rows only (Macaulay row counts per equation), since the matrices do not fit.
ideas.math: System: m-1 equations, each n F2-coordinate polynomials; unknowns N_p = ml + (m-2)n. Of the (m-1)n equations, (m-2)n are R-independent. Macaulay degree D rows: t * g for monomials t with deg t <= D - deg g; row count is proportional to the equation count when the degrees match, so the R-independent fraction of rows is (m-2)/(m-1): 1/2 (m=3), 2/3 (m=4), 3/4 (m=5), 7/8 (m=8), 18/19 (m=20). Dense F2 elimination of a rows x cols matrix of rank r costs about rows*cols*r/64 word-ops; with the shared echelon stored, a new target needs only new_rows * cols * r_shared/64 plus the elimination of the residual new rows, so gain -> rows/new_rows = m-1 as rank saturates. Corrections: the stored echelon is denser than raw rows (fill), so the sparse-kernel gain is below m-1: this is why the claim interval is [1.2, m-1], not exactly m-1. Amortisation: shared cost / T + per-target cost, T targets (or T = n conjugates per target); at T = 131 conjugates the shared cost vanishes. Memory: the shared echelon is stored once; the largest F4 matrix on record is 84,355 x 66,607 at (11,4) with 1.0-1.5 GB RSS, and (13,4), (13,5) hit the 3 GB cap, so a smaller per-target active set may also move the memory wall in README.md of research/ic_next10_20261014/06-equivariant-f4-m4/.
ideas.why_closure_does_not_apply: C5 concerns equivariant elimination and the 5.1x/15.5x oracle ratios. This idea does not claim equivariant elimination; it uses the equivariance (Proposition T, C4) only to turn n conjugate bases into n targets over one base, which C4 permits. Nothing in the closure addresses cross-target reuse of reduced Macaulay rows. The 0.29-0.59x regression of arm F on production-shaped systems is about appending the root's fall rows to every node's generators, not about reusing a precomputed echelon of the target-independent part, and the two have different costs per node. The mismatch with the user's m remark is deliberate: the gain is linear in m-1 with a built-in m=2 null.

Arms per cell (m, n, l), 20 random targets plus all n conjugates of 2 targets: (A) full Macaulay pass per target (control); (B) precomputed shared echelon + incremental reduction per target; (C) A/A; (D) m=2 negative control. Measures: row-space and refutation-bit equality with A (exact), thread-CPU ratio A/B per target, amortised ratio including the one-off shared cost for T = 20 and T = n. Price all arms at 0, 0.1, 1 GAE (AGENTS.md 5a). Cost: seconds to minutes per cell at n <= 13; no msolve needed (degree-3 and -4 XL passes only; F4 pair selection is not reproduced).

The m-scaling prediction fails if the ratio is flat in m across m=3..6. No Lean obligation beyond the linearity of the final link in r_k, which is already in polynomial_reuse.rs; the row-space equality is a computational check.

ideas.title: Price the equivariant block at the n=131 endpoint: F_{2^130} / R_131 arithmetic calibration (the missing pen(d) factor)
ideas.mechanism: Every gain formula in the equivariant stack carries pen(d), the cost of an F_{2^d} (or R_n) multiply-accumulate relative to an F2 word XOR: RESEARCH_G2_EQUIVARIANT_F4_SCOPE.md section 3 gives gain ~ n^2 d / (rho^3 * 64 * pen(d)) and quotes about 300x at n=131 (d=130) with 'three-word carry-less multiplies' as an assumption. All measured block timings use d <= 18 (n=11..23) with log/antilog tables, and n=31 uses d=5. At n=131 a single nontrivial block over F_{2^130} replaces six or eighteen small Galois-orbit blocks, tables do not exist, and the arithmetic is a 3x3-word carry-less product plus reduction. The extrapolation to the actual target field is therefore unmeasured. Because R_131 = F2 x F_{2^130}, multiplication can be done as a cyclic convolution of 131-bit vectors (9 PCLMUL + wrap) with no separate modular reduction by Phi_131; the trivial block rides along in the same ring.
ideas.exact_claim: A native dense Gauss-Jordan on random B x B' blocks over F_{2^130} (represented as 3 u64 words, B between 256 and 2048) achieves a multiply-accumulate cost of at most 80 F2-word-XOR-equivalents per entry operation (pen <= 80), and the dense fold factor n^3/(64*pen) at n=131 is then between 2^8 and 2^11. Complement: at the same dimension the unfolded F2 control scaled from measured n <= 23 timings has exponent between 2.5 and 3.0.
ideas.m_regime: Block arithmetic is independent of m. m enters only through the block dimension B (orbit columns of the symmetric system): about C(N_s,<=D)/131 = 6.2e8 at m=4, n=131, l=33, D=4 (idea 1 count), so the calibration is run at B = 256..2048 and extrapolated with the measured exponent; no run at the true B is claimed.
ideas.math: Unfolded dense F2 elimination of an (nB) x (nB) matrix costs about (nB)^3/64 word-ops; folded dense elimination costs B^3 * pen word-ops, so the dense fold factor is n^3/(64*pen). At n=131: 2.25e6/(64*pen) = 3.5e4/pen. With pen=20: 1.8e3 (2^10.8); pen=80: 440 (2^8.8). For comparison the measured 44x / 58x / 73x at n = 11 / 13 / 17 are against a naive bit-packed kernel, and 2-3x against the crate kernel at d=8..12, which suggests the dense model overstates by one to two orders of magnitude unless sparsity of the control is accounted for; the calibration therefore must also report the control's measured exponent. Entry cost: 9 PCLMULQDQ (about 9-18 cycles) + 6-8 shift/XOR for the wrap + 3 XOR accumulate = 20-30 cycles, against 0.25-0.5 cycles per 64-bit F2 word-XOR, giving pen(entry) of 40-120 in cycle terms, so the interval pen <= 80 is a genuine prediction that could fail.
ideas.why_closure_does_not_apply: C5's 'a constant only' is a statement about measured ratios at n <= 13..23 and d <= 18, together with a naive-versus-gf2_elim correction. It does not measure d=130 arithmetic, and it does not price the ratio at the target field. The closure also never states the endpoint constant; it needs it, because the ranking across arms must hold across the 0 / 0.1 / 1 GAE pricing band (AGENTS.md 5a) and pen is one of the unpriced native operations. This idea does not change the closure's verdict on production applicability; it replaces an extrapolated constant by a measured one.
ideas.cheapest_test: Native Rust microbenchmark, no Python: (1) R_131 cyclic multiply with core::arch::x86_64 PCLMULQDQ, (2) dense row elimination kernel over F_{2^130} for B in {256, 512, 1024, 2048}, (3) timing of the inverse (once per pivot, extended Euclid or Fermat in F_{2^130}), (4) control: crate gf2_elim on random F2 matrices of dimension 131*B for the sizes that fit (B <= 100), to fit the control exponent; (5) the same kernel at d=10, 12, 18 using tables to anchor against the on-disk block timings (n=11: 0.05-0.06 s, n=19: 0.64 s CPU for the 3,835 x 8,344 block). Thread CPU, A/A, same process. Cost: minutes. Report pen with a 95% bootstrap CI and the implied 2^k fold factor at n=131 for pen at its CI endpoints.
ideas.falsification: Killed (the model's constant is wrong) if pen > 200 at B >= 512, which would put the dense fold factor below 2^7.5 and below the +7.6 to +9.8 bit gap of the m=4 route, or if the anchor runs at d=10,12,18 disagree with the on-disk timings by more than 30% (then the kernel, not the field size, is mis-specified). If pen <= 40 the dense fold factor exceeds 2^10.7 and idea 1's break-even condition gets a new bound. This idea creates no new mathematical claim to Lean-formalise beyond the ring isomorphism R_131 = F2 x F_{2^130}, which ord_131(2)=130 gives directly.

ideas.title: Probe-prefix asymmetry in the pair-table oracle: up to C(m,2)-fold fewer probes per distinct relation, m=3 in production and m=4..8 in a nested-probe oracle
ideas.mechanism: The production pair-table oracle runs only m in {2,3}: src/cryptanalysis/ic_boundary.rs lines 6386-6446 (decompose_mitm and the Frobenius twin) and the table in src/cryptanalysis/ic_framework/plugins.rs lines 31-41 (mitm '2 or 3'; chained-x is the only m=4 route). For m=3 it loops over ALL fb.points (B probes of R-P_i against the pair table) and returns at the first hit. An unordered m-set S is reachable from C(m,2) different (probe digits, pair) splits (3 at m=3), so S_m acts on the probe loop as pure redundancy. Restricting the probe digits to a prefix F_0 of size rho*B, with the pair table still over all of F, breaks that symmetry by ROLE. No Frobenius is used: the slots are distinguished because probe slots and pair slots draw from different sets. This is the same effect that the tau-Horner lead (LEAD-ICB-tau-horner-chain, open_next_step) credits to Frobenius. It also predicts that the lead's own null arm (IDEA-20261018-f2cd4d) is incomplete. 'Plain + lex SB' there removes (m-2)! probe orderings but not the C(m,2) choice of which two summands form the pair. Closest published: Galbraith-Gebregiyorgis, ePrint 2014/806 (factor base that breaks symmetry), Diem's disjoint cosets (KN-LIT-71b758 C3), and early-abort in index calculus (a search found no source for probe-subset truncation in a pair-table oracle, so novelty is unverified). What differs: the lever is applied to the table-probe loop that the production m=3 rows use (candidate names '...PDP3pairtable...' under research/ic_tool_program/rule/v8/manifests/candidates/), priced per distinct relation. Risks: rank or column-coverage bias, because columns in F\F_0 enter relations only through the pair; per-target overhead when rho*B is small; the production sizing may already sit at nu>=10, where the gain is about 1.
ideas.exact_claim: Let B=|F| (signed base points), nu = expected distinct m-subsets of F summing to a random target = C(B,m)/|E| (|E|=4r on ECC2K-type curves). ideas.title: Algebraic pair tail: for m >= sqrt(2n) the last two summands are an F_2-linear system in (e_1,e_2); a memory-free pair table and a regime map for large m
ideas.mechanism: The Semaev S_3 form for y^2+xy=x^3+1 (b=1) is S3(a,b,c)=a^2b^2+a^2c^2+b^2c^2+abc+1. With e1=b+c, e2=bc it equals e2^2 + a*e2 + a^2*e1^2 + 1. For fixed a=x(X) this is F_2-affine in the bits of (e1,e2), since squaring is linear. With b,c in a l-dimensional subspace V, e1 is in V (l bits) and e2 is in V.V (at most l(l+1)/2 formal coordinates), so there are l(l+3)/2 unknown bits against n equations. When l(l+3)/2 <= n a single GF(2) elimination decides whether a pair with x(b),x(c) in V sums to +-X, and returns it (recover b from u=e1, s_ij = b_i u_j + b_j u_i, s_ii = b_i(1+u_i), also linear). The S_2-symmetrised form needs l(l+3)/2 <= n, the distinct-shift (Horner) pair S3(a, b^{2^s}, c^{2^t}) is bilinear with l^2+2l unknowns. So the tail of a Semaev chain is polynomial time exactly when m >= about sqrt(2n) (n=131: m>=10 at l=13, or m>=13 for distinct shifts at l=10), a regime NO program cell has reached. Every toy ladder in LEAD-ICB-decomposition-encoding-and-sat (lines 16-22: WDSat 2.9985 bits per unit l at m=3, alpha 4.09-4.33 at m=4, 'no arm grows slower than the enumeration floor') sits at m<=4, i.e. l(l+3)/2 > n, so that floor was never tested where the linear tail applies. Closest published: FPPR (Eurocrypt 2012, e_i variables), Petit-Quisquater (m about sqrt(n) first-fall-degree regime), Joux-Vitse hybrid. What differs here is the exact linear-algebra threshold for the S_2 tail, priced as a memory-free substitute for the pair claw the program already uses (src/cryptanalysis/ic_framework/plugins.rs). I expect this to tie the pair claw on relations per probe and lose on time per probe; its value is as the regime map for m>4 and as the encoding that gives a SAT/XOR solver the structure it misses.
ideas.exact_claim: At toy cells with l(l+3)/2 <= n, the hybrid 'enumerate m-2 summands, solve the final pair by one GF(2) elimination of the n x l(l+3)/2 system plus the linear recovery of (b,c)' returns exactly the relation set of an exhaustive search, performs C(B,m-2) tail solves, and each solve costs about n*l(l+3)/2 /64 word operations. Per distinct relation this is 2|E|/B^2 solves with role-asymmetric probes (m(m-1)|E|/B^2 with sorted probes), identical to a pair table of B^2/2 entries at zero memory. When l(l+3)/2 > n the candidate count is 2^(l(l+3)/2 - rank), and the hybrid loses to enumeration once that excess exceeds 2(l+1) bits. Lean obligations: (i) the ring identity S3(a,b,c)=e2^2+a*e2+a^2*e1^2+b in characteristic 2 (a one-line proof by 'ring' after char-2 normalisation); (ii) F_2-linearity of (e1,e2) -> e2^2+a*e2+a^2*e1^2; (iii) uniqueness of (b,c) from (u,s) when u != 0.
ideas.math: Counts: unknown bits l(l+3)/2: l=3 ->9, l=4 ->14, l=5 ->20, l=6 ->27, l=13 ->104, l=14 ->119. Threshold l(l+3)/2 <= n gives l <= 4 at n=19 (l=5: 20 > 19 fails by one), l <= 5 at n=23..31 (l=6: 27 > 23 and 27 <= 31 holds, so l=6 works at n>=27), l <= 14 at n=131. Hybrid work against the floor at m=3, n=3l: exponent l+1 + max(0, l(l+3)/2 - 3l) versus the WDSat law 3l - log2(3!); the hybrid wins only for l <= 6, i.e. n <= 18, which is why the ladders n=11..31 at m=3 and m=4 never saw it. At m=4, n=4l the same comparison gives hybrid < floor for l <= 7, i.e. n <= 28. Worked cell n=31, m=8, l=4: B about 16, |E|~2^31; sorted probes C(16,6)=8008 tail solves, exhaustive sorted 8-subsets C(16,8)=12870, Horner distinct shifts (needs l^2+2l=24 <= 31) B^6=2^24 tail solves for nu_H=B^8/|E|=2. Per relation: 55 times better for distinct shifts than sorted probes, matching m(m-1)=56. Boundary: total cost to collect B relations is >= 2|E|/B, with B <= 2^sqrt(2n) by the threshold. At n=131 that is 2^118 against matched rho 2^60.8, a gap of about 2^57. So this cannot beat the matched rho; it is memory-free pair-claw accounting.

It tests a different premise: the lead's statement that no arm beats the enumeration floor, which was measured only at m<=4. With distinct Frobenius shifts on the two tail slots the tail is bilinear (l^2+2l unknowns), but the shifts are applied to fixed variables inside one system, and no conjugate-target equivariance is invoked.

Stage 2: for planted and natural relations, check that the hybrid returns exactly the exhaustive relation set (completeness), count tail solves, and compare with the pair-table oracle on the same cells (probes, lookups, memory). Stage 3: price each arm at 0/0.1/1 GAE per op (section 5a) and report the ratio to matched rho-frob. The SAT stage is killed if conflicts do not fall by at least 2^(l/2) relative to the plain chain at m>=5.

ideas.title: Pattern-breadth independence and the sharing deficit of per-slot Frobenius shift unions, with exact system counts D(n,m) up to m=10
ideas.mechanism: A per-slot shift pattern k=(k_1..k_m) in (Z/n)^m means R = sum tau^{k_i} Q_i with Q_i in F; the descended system is the plain chain with slot i over sigma^{k_i}(V). Patterns with pairwise distinct shifts have no slot symmetry. The S_m orbit of a pattern is only a relabelling, and the common shift is NOT a gauge for a fixed R (it moves R to sigma^j R). Each such pattern has the same expected relation count nu_pat = |F|^m/|E|. If solver cost is additive over patterns, the cost per relation is independent of the number of patterns, so a union over D patterns can only win through SHARING between patterns. The measured m=2 data (KN-FIND-47da4e: conflict ratios 1.017, 1.017, 1.467, 1.150 at n=13, 17, 19, 23 against the sum of the gauge-fixed systems) show no sharing. No m>=3 cell exists. In the table regime sharing is total, because one lookup in the orbit-folded pair table covers all n^2 shift pairs (mitm-frobenius, plugins.rs line 37), which is the T*M law gain of n. So the question is whether a SAT/XOR solver has any such sharing at m=3..6. Closest: GGMP (ePrint 2020/1315, Frobenius-closed factor bases, n^2 linear-algebra gain) and the KN-FIND-47da4e pilot. Different: exact quotient count and the additivity theorem as the null. Remark from the audit: the only targets with a genuine Z/n stabiliser are R in E(F_2) (4 points, cofactor part), which meets the lead's revisit_when trigger literally, but the accounting identity is unchanged: a stabilised target gives nu/n rows at 1/n of the gauge cost, so cost per row is the same.
ideas.exact_claim: (1) For a prime n and m<n, Z/n acts freely on size-m multisets of shifts, so the number of distinct pattern classes is D(n,m)=C(n+m-1,m)/n, not n^{m-1}; the ratio n^{m-1}/D tends to m! (111.3 at n=131, m=5; about 2^21 at m=10, where D(131,10) is about 2^42.3). (2) Under additivity, per-relation cost of any family of patterns with distinct shifts equals that of one pattern. (3) Measured claim: on the chained S3 SAT (binary_semaev_chain_sat.rs) at n in {11,13} and m in {3,4,5}, the sharing ratio S = conflicts(one-hot union over all sorted patterns) / sum over patterns of conflicts(single pattern) lies in [1.0, 1.5]. Lean obligations: (a) free action and the orbit count D(n,m) (Burnside, Fermat for n prime); (b) per-pattern relation count identity nu_pat=|F|^m/|E| holds as an expectation over random targets; (c) the additivity corollary is arithmetic and does not need a proof.

ideas.math: D(n,m)=C(n+m-1,m)/n. n=7: D(7,2)=4, D(7,3)=12, D(7,4)=30. n=11: D(11,3)=26, D(11,4)=91, D(11,5)=273. n=13: D(13,4)=140. n=17,m=2: 9 against n^{m-1}=17 (the audit figure). n=131: D(131,5)=C(135,5)/131 = 317,588,040/120 = 2,646,567 against 131^4=294,499,921 (ratio 111.3); D(131,10) about 2^42.3. Per pattern: nu_pat=B^m/|E| (|F|=B, ordered by role), against B^m/(m!|E|) for the plain subspace; so a pattern with all-distinct shifts buys m! in yield at identical descended shape, and the union of all D patterns reproduces |F~|^m/(m!|E|) with |F~|=nB, since D*B^m/|E| about n^{m-1}B^m/(m!|E|). Sign group: x-only chained S3 returns exactly one chain model per true sign pattern (the number of eps in {+-1}^{m-1} with sum eps_i P_i = +-R is 1 for a true relation), so the 2^{m-1} sign multiplicity does not inflate model counts. Per-slot shifts that are not applied uniformly are not symmetries of a fixed target at any m (they require sum (lambda^{k_i}-1)P_i=0, probability about 1/r), which is Lemma A1's consequence.
ideas.why_closure_does_not_apply: C3 states orbit encodings cost >=0.95x the plain search at n=17,23,31, but its source is a pre-registered threshold (H-BINSTD-c72284, Stage 2 unauthorised) and the real data (KN-FIND-47da4e) are m=2 against the SUM of n gauge-fixed systems. ideas.title: S_m as a refutation-proof multiplier: complete leaf-sorting (and a balanced-tree encoding that makes the symmetry visible) on chained-S3 SAT at m = 2..8
ideas.mechanism: Fix any target R and base F. The group S_m (order m!) permutes the m summands and fixes (R,F) at every m and every n, including n=131, so it is a genuine single-target stabiliser. In the chained-S3 encoding it is NOT a variable permutation, because a permutation of leaves changes every partial sum, so generic symmetry-detection tools (BreakID/Shatter) cannot see it. In a balanced binary tree the m-1 node swaps ARE variable permutations (subtree swaps, group Z2 wr ... of order 2^(m-1)), and a leaf-sorted constraint x_1 <= x_2 <= ... <= x_m (m-1 l-bit comparators) is a complete lex-leader breaker for the whole S_m. Most IC trials are refutations (hit rate 0.3-0.6 at toy n; about 1-e^-lambda in general), and symmetric UNSAT proofs inflate by up to the group order (Haken-style pigeonhole behaviour; Crawford et al. lex-leader 1996). The earlier null (lex tried only at m<=3, n<=15) cannot see an effect that scales like (m!)^beta. This is the precise, testable form of the owner's 'group grows with m' intuition for the part of the group that really grows.
ideas.exact_claim: Let B(m) = median conflicts-to-UNSAT of plain chained-S3 / median of the same CNF plus complete leaf-sorting, over >=20 planted-UNSAT draws per cell (targets certified non-decomposable by exact enumeration). H0 (CDCL already absorbs S_m, no lever): B(m) <= 1.3 for every m <= 8. H1 (owner-style growth): B(6) >= 5 and B(m) increases monotonically in m. The known point is B(3) about 1.16 (5512 vs 6412 conflicts at m=3, n=9, from the audit synthesis; no file path found for that run in this read-only pass). A fit B(m) = (m!)^beta gives beta about 0.083 from that point, predicting B(6) about 1.7 and B(8) about 1.9, which is H0-compatible. Report beta with a CI. Secondary claim: the balanced-tree encoding plus automatic detection reproduces the sorted-leaf B(m) within a factor 1.5 (so the lever is encoding-visible, not tool-specific).

Model counting identity: #models(plain chain) = (#ordered solutions) because intermediates are determined = m! x #distinct-leaf multisets + degenerate; #models(sorted) = #multisets. These identities are exact and checkable by brute force (n=13, l=4, m=4: 2^16 leaf tuples). Comparator cost: (m-1) l-bit comparators, about 3l clauses each, negligible next to the (m-2)n-bit chain. Lean obligation: 'a model of the chain CNF exists iff a leaf-sorted model exists' (S_m acts on leaf tuples, the sorted tuple is a transversal of the orbit; the chain is functional in the leaves). Closest published: Galbraith-Gebregiyorgis 2014 (ia.cr/2014/806) choose a factor base that BREAKS the symmetry and report 'not conclusive'; Faugere et al. FGHR (J. Cryptol 2014) exploit S_m through invariants in F4, not in SAT. Neither tests S_m breaking for UNSAT-dominated SAT trials at m>3.

S_m is a genuine stabiliser for every fixed R, so none of C1-C4 speaks to it. C5 is about equivariant F4 at m=2. The only prior S_m evidence is lex-breaking at m<=3, n<=15 (audit synthesis), which has group order <=6 and cannot reveal super-linear growth. LEAD-ICB-decomposition-encoding-and-sat is the nearest lead and treats the SAT route as exhausted as an EXPONENT lead; this proposal asks only a constant-factor, m-scaling question and says so.

ideas.title: Representation-multiplicity (clumping) law for the (Z/2)^m x S_m group at m = 2..8: exact census, compound-Poisson hit rate, Fano factor 2^(m-1), and triviality after cofactor projection
ideas.mechanism: On a base closed under +T (u -> u+1 in the u = 1/(x+1) frame; src/cryptanalysis/koblitz_symmetrised.rs:229-238 shows V need not be Frobenius-stable, only 1 in V), the even-weight translation group (Z/2)^(m-1) fixes R exactly (order 2^m on the class {R, R+T}) and acts freely on the representations of R. Hence n_rep(R) is a multiple of 2^(m-1), the number of distinct orbits is Poisson(lambda / 2^(m-1)) and P(hit) = 1 - exp(-lambda/2^(m-1)). That is a TAX of exactly the group order on hit rate that grows exponentially in m, while the benefit (columns halved, m-1 fewer unknown bits) grows linearly. After cofactor projection [4] the translation T is trivial (4T = O), so a projected base has no T structure at all; the only reason T helps algebraic oracles is that they need a linear description of the base in E rather than in Z/r. The program has the law at m=2 (hit 0.317 vs 0.604, trials per relation 3.26 vs 1.71, research/koblitz_symmetrised_e2e_20260927/RESULTS.md) and m=3 at n=31 (hit 0.207 vs 0.444 and the 2^(m-1) multiplicity, research/isogeny_fibers_20261010/parts/p7b_a1_results.md lines 17-42). Nothing at m>=4, and the Fano-factor signature of free action was never measured.
ideas.exact_claim: For a T-closed, negation-closed base of N points with all x_i distinct classes: (i) n_rep(R) = 0 mod 2^(m-1) for every R (exact, deterministic); (ii) Var/Mean of n_rep(R) over R in the whole group equals 2^(m-1) (+/-5 percent) once coincident-class tuples (a lower-order term of relative size O(m^2/N)) are excluded; (iii) the measured fraction of decomposable targets matches 1 - exp(-lambda/2^(m-1)) within sampling error for m = 2..8, where lambda = N^m/(m! #E) is calibrated on a T-free x-frame base of the same size; (iv) a cofactor-projected x-frame base and the projected image of the T-closed base have identical decomposable fractions (difference < 2 percent). Consequence stated as a prediction: for a meet-in-the-middle oracle at equal points the cost per hit worsens by 2^(m/2-1) (1, 1.41, 2, 2.8, 4, 8 at m = 2,3,4,5,6,8), matching the measured 1.18-1.28 at m=3 (n=31); at equal columns T-closure and projection are the same gain.

Free-action count: E[#orbits] = E[n_rep]/|G_free| where G_free = 2^(m-1) (the m! is already in lambda because the baseline counts multisets). Numerics at n=31 m=3 from the isogeny report: lambda_x = -ln(1-0.444) = 0.587; u-base has 2357 vs 2049 points, so lambda_u = 0.587 x (2357/2049)^3 / 4 = 0.223, hit = 0.200 vs measured 0.207/0.219. So the law already predicts the m=3 point to about 5 percent (the report's 0.38-vs-0.47 gap is Poisson saturation). Closest published: FGHR (J. Cryptol 2014) and Faugere-Huot-Joux-Renault-Vitse (Eurocrypt 2014) symmetrise with the 2-torsion for the degree/solve gain and do not account for the hit-rate tax; Galbraith-Gebregiyorgis 2014 observe symmetry-breaking bases increase relation probability but report no law.

This is the translation half of the owner's group (2-torsion), which LEAD-ICB-cofactor-torsion-quotients closes only for 'subspace x-frame bases on prime-degree curves' (its corrected iota-stable classification) and notes FGHR symmetrisation is 'a separate constant'. The u-frame T-closed base exists at n=131 for any V containing 1 (koblitz_symmetrised.rs:229-238), so that cell is not empty in the u-frame, and no ledger result gives its m-scaling. A pass means the T-lever is closed at every tested m for combinatorial oracles and quantifies the per-trial speed-up an algebraic oracle must exceed.

ideas.title: Odd abelian subgroups of S_m as an equivariant-F4 stabiliser that grows exponentially in m: C_3^floor(m/3) character blocks, rank-only ratios at m = 3, 6 (9 optional)
ideas.mechanism: Faugere-Svartz (ISSAC 2013, 'Groebner bases of ideals invariant under a commutative group: the non-modular case') needs an abelian group whose order is prime to the characteristic, so in characteristic 2 only the ODD part of a symmetry group can be block-diagonalised; (Z/2)^m translations and the 2-part of S_m are unusable by this route. S_m has large odd abelian subgroups: disjoint 3-cycles give A = C_3^k, k = floor(m/3), |A| = 3^k = 3, 9, 27, 81, 729 at m = 3, 6, 9, 12, 18 (exponential, about 1.44^m), and they are genuine stabilisers of (R,F) for every fixed R and every V. A acts on the Boolean unknowns c_(i,t) by permuting slot blocks, so it acts on squarefree monomials by permutations with almost no fixed points; the Macaulay matrices at each degree are A-stable, and over F_4 (2 has order 2 mod 3) they split into |A| isotypic blocks of size about M/|A|. Unlike the 2^(m-1) translation group (clumping tax) there is NO yield tax, because the baseline hit rate already counts multisets (the 1/m! in lambda). So the per-trial gain is not cancelled. The audit synthesis already names C_3 at m=3,4 and the 3-6x smaller blocks; the new content is the exponential growth of the usable odd group with m and an exact count of how much of it survives as free orbits.
ideas.exact_claim: For the m-slot decomposition system (chained or direct S_(m+1)) with A = C_3^k acting on slots: (1) the number of A-orbits of squarefree degree-D monomials is within 6 percent of C(ml,D)/|A| for D <= l+3 (exact by Burnside); (2) the sum over characters of block ranks equals the rank of the full degree-D Macaulay matrix (exact identity over F_4, a bit-for-bit check on every sampled instance); (3) the total word-XOR count of block elimination (F_4 arithmetic priced at the measured cost of an F_4 multiply in word ops) is at most 0.5 x the crate gf2_elim count on the same matrix at m=6, |A|=9, and at most 1.0x at m=3 (|A|=3), so the gain grows with m. Prediction: ratio (blocks/gf2_elim) in [0.15, 0.5] at m=6 and [0.7, 1.3] at m=3.
ideas.m_regime: m = 3 (A=C_3), m = 6 (A=C_3 x C_3, also C_5 on 5 slots as a second group), optional m = 9 (|A|=27) if the wide-mask engine exists (the current equivariant oracle is capped at 64-bit monomials). n = 13..19, l = 4..6, degrees D up to l+2 (the measured refutation degree is about l+2, research/ic_symmetry_lever_slope_20260929/RESULTS.md).
ideas.math: Worked count, m=6, l=4 (24 Boolean unknowns), D=6, A = <(123),(456)> acting by block permutation. C(24,6) = 134,596 monomials. Fixed monomials: identity 134,596; the 4 elements acting as a single 3-cycle on one triple fix sum_j C(4,j) C(12,6-3j) = 924+880+6 = 1,810 each; the 4 elements acting on both triples fix C(8,2) = 28 each. Orbits = (134,596 + 4 x 1,810 + 4 x 28)/9 = 141,948/9 = 15,772, i.e. a 8.53x reduction (free would be 9x). m=3, l=6 (18 unknowns), D=5: C(18,5) = 8,568, 3 does not divide 5 so no fixed monomials, orbits 2,856 exactly (3.00x). Cost model for dense elimination: |A| blocks of size M/r (r = 8.53): time ratio = |A| r^(-omega) c_ext. omega=2: 9/72.8 = 0.124; omega=2.4: 9/170 = 0.053; with c_ext about 3 for F_4 versus F_2 packed arithmetic these become 0.37 and 0.16, i.e. 2.7x and 6.3x. At |A|=3 the same model gives 3/(3^omega) x 3 = 1.0 (omega=2) so no gain: this reproduces the repo's finding that the equivariant kernel is only 2-3x against gf2_elim at group order about n. Lean obligations: (a) F_2[A] is semisimple for |A| odd (Maschke) so the Macaulay row space decomposes into isotypic components; (b) rank(M) = sum over irreducible F_2[A]-modules of multiplicity x rank of the block (a linear-algebra lemma). Closest published: Faugere-Svartz 2013 (commutative, non-modular); Faugere-Rahmany 2009 (SAGBI) and FGHR use S_m through invariants and degree drop, not character blocks in the Boolean-descent regime.
ideas.why_closure_does_not_apply: C5 evidence is Frobenius characters, m=2, l=3, n<=13, and the 'does not apply to production' point is about the Frobenius pass on production pair tables. This group is a slot permutation, fixes every single target R (the revisit_when clause 'a genuine stabilizer of a single target R in the descended system' is literally met), needs no Frobenius-stable V (it works at n=131), and has no m=2 analogue (C_3 needs m>=3). The closure also does not say the barrel (production re-presentation) must be non-equivariant. Honest scope: algebraic oracles sit at about 10^6-10^7 x rho at n=31 in the program's own e2e table, so this can change a constant in a component far from rho; it does not touch Table A rows.
ideas.cheapest_test: Native Rust, rank-only and exact (the same scope as RESEARCH_G2_EQUIVARIANT_F4_SCOPE.md). Step 1 (counting only): Burnside orbit counts for A in {C_3 (m=3), C_3^2 (m=6), C_5 (m=5), C_3 x C_5 (m=8)} against C(ml,D); no linear algebra. Step 2: build the degree-D Macaulay matrix of the chained-S3 and the direct S_(m+1) systems for 10 planted-UNSAT and 10 SAT draws per cell (n=13,17; m=3,6), eliminate once with the crate gf2_elim (control) and once as A-blocks over F_4, verify rank identity, report word XORs. Arms: (a) crate gf2_elim; (b) A-blocks; (c) A-blocks + fall-row augmentation (it supplied 11.6 of the 15.5x in the Frobenius oracle, so it must be applied equally to (a) to avoid the same attribution error); (d) naive kernel as a diagnostic only. Priced in counted word XORs; the F_4 multiply cost is measured, not assumed; ratios across arms at 0, 0.1, 1 GAE/op unpriced native work per 5a (hash/index build included). Needs a Conductor task and resume checkpoint.
ideas.falsification: Any of: orbit reduction below 0.7 |A| at D <= l+2 (fixed monomials dominate, the premise of near-free orbits fails); a rank-identity mismatch (bug or wrong decomposition); block cost ratio >= 0.8 at m=6 against a gf2_elim that also gets fall-row augmentation (then the odd part of S_m is the same 'constant only' result as Frobenius and the lead's equivariant clause should extend to it); or block cost ratio not smaller at m=6 than at m=3 (no growth with m).

ideas.title: The one place Frobenius is a genuine stabiliser: closed sums with R in E(F_2) on a sigma-stable base, yield tax n versus equivariant gain n^(omega-1)/c_ext
ideas.mechanism: For a target R in E(F_2) = {O, T, g, -g} (equivalently t = 0 after cofactor projection) we have sigma(R) = R, so on a sigma-stable base V the tau-orbit IS a stabiliser of the single instance S_m(x_1..x_m) = 0 (or S_(m+1)(x_1..x_m, x(R)) = 0 with x(R) in {0,1}), the only target class for which C1 fails. These are the free (target-free, homogeneous) relations. A solution orbit of size n (2n with sign) gives ONE relation row up to the scalar lambda, so the yield per solution is 1/(n) (tax n), exactly the clumping law of the T-group. The benefit is a graded Macaulay matrix: over F_(2^k) with k = ord_n(2) the unknowns split into eigen-coordinates on which sigma acts by weights 2^j, so the degree-D matrix splits into n weight blocks of size M/n (n odd, so Faugere-Svartz non-modular applies; the repo's Frobenius equivariant oracle is the same construction but at fixed target). The question is whether the per-trial speed-up n^(omega-1)/c_ext beats the tax n; the net is n^(omega-2)/c_ext, which is below 1 for omega < 2 + log_n(c_ext).
ideas.exact_claim: On sigma-stable V (n = 31 dims 5, 10; n = 23 dim 11; n = 15 exploratory) with R in E(F_2): (1) every solution orbit under <sigma> x <-1> has size 2n (free) except the sigma-fixed points inside V = F_2, and relation rows from one orbit are scalar multiples in the orbit basis (exact); (2) the number of independent homogeneous relations per found solution is 1/(2n) (+/-10 percent, measured by rank of rows from a full enumeration at n=15, 31); (3) the weight-graded block elimination of the degree-D Macaulay matrix has cost ratio vs gf2_elim in [n^-(omega-1) c, ...] i.e. predicted 0.05-0.3 at n=31; (4) therefore NET cost per independent relation = (block cost ratio) x (2n) is in [0.8, 3] and the lever does not beat the unconstrained single-trial baseline. This predicts a null and is a calibration of the closure's C3/C5 from the only side where the stabiliser is real.
ideas.m_regime: closed sums with m = 3, 4 slots (m=5 if n=31, l=5 and degree <= 6), n = 15, 23, 31 where stable V exist (at n=131, V is only F_2 or the whole field, so this cannot be a direct ECC2K-130 route; only the nonlinear stable bases lead (LEAD-ICB-nonlinear-frob-stable-bases) could supply a stable set there)
ideas.math: Group <sigma> x <-1> x (odd abelian part of S_m) acting on a closed instance; order 2n x |A|. n=31: sigma acts on a dimension-5 irreducible V as multiplication by a root alpha of a quintic, order 31, so over F_32 each slot has 5 eigen-coordinates with weights 2^j mod 31 and every monomial has a weight in Z/31; the Macaulay matrix is Z/31-graded and block sizes are M/31 up to fixed-weight monomials. Orbit count of ordered solutions = (#solutions)/(2n m!) for the multiset. Required number of solutions for a full-rank orbit-basis system: columns C = |F|/(2n), rows C, each row = one orbit => total solutions needed about 2n C = |F|, so N^(m-1) >= m! r (N = |F|): at n=31, r about 2^20, m=4: N >= (24 x 2^20)^(1/3) about 300, i.e. l >= 9 (dim 10 stable). Net model: gain per trial n^(omega-1)/c_ext (omega=2: 31/6 = 5.2; omega=2.4: 3.7e... 31^1.4=122, /6 = 20), tax 2n = 62, net 0.08-0.33 of baseline cost-per-row would be a LOSS (ratio > 1 means worse; here the cost-per-row ratio is 62/(5.2 to 20) = 3 to 12 x worse), unless fall-row augmentation or lower c_ext intervenes. Lean obligation: for R in E(F_2) and sigma-stable F the map sigma permutes the representation set of R freely modulo fixed points (orbit-counting lemma; sigma has order n on E(F_(2^n)) and fixes only E(F_2)).
ideas.why_closure_does_not_apply: C1 and C2 are about FIXED targets with sigma(R) != R; here sigma(R) = R, which is exactly the revisit_when clause 'a genuine stabilizer of a single target R', and the ledger has no cost measurement for target-free closed sums with Frobenius quotient (the free-relation line LEAD-ICB-free-relations-self-collision harvests them by sorting the pair-root table, not by solving a quotient system, and found rank 49 of 588 rows at n61/K600). C3's '>= 0.95x' is a pre-registered threshold for the fixed-target orbit-union encoding (m=2, n=13..23 only), not this instance class.
ideas.cheapest_test: Native Rust, exact enumeration first. (1) At n = 15 and n = 23 (stable V) enumerate all solutions of the closed system by brute force over V^m (<= 2^33 at worst; use meet-in-the-middle for m=4), compute orbit sizes under <sigma, -1>, rank of the orbit-basis relation matrix, and rows per solution; control: the same count for a random target (Frobenius is an equivariance there, expected multiplicity 1, i.e. no clumping). (2) At n = 31, dim 5 and 10, m=3,4: degree-D Macaulay matrices, graded-block versus gf2_elim word XORs (reuse the existing equivariant oracle with R fixed to O instead of a random target and a stable V; no new algebra). Arms: gf2_elim; weight-graded blocks; blocks + fall-row augmentation applied to BOTH sides; unquotiented plain solve. Report net cost per independent relation = block cost x (solutions per independent row). Priced in counted XORs; unpriced native ops (hash, dlog table) at 0, 0.1, 1 GAE/op per 5a. Needs Conductor + resume checkpoint.
ideas.falsification: Net cost per independent relation <= 0.8 x the unquotiented baseline at n=31 (then Frobenius as a genuine stabiliser pays and the closure's equivariant clause needs a target-free exception, which would raise the priority of finding stable non-subspace bases at n=131). Or (1) fails: relation rows per solution differ from 1/(2n) by more than 25 percent (then the free-action premise is wrong and the correlation seen in the production free-relation harvest has another cause). A net ratio between 0.8 and 3 is the expected null and should be recorded as the calibration of the C3 constant at the one place where the stabiliser exists.

Notation: n = field degree, m = summand count (AGENTS.md 8a uses 'm' for field degree; its n=83 gate is also absent from this plan). All arithmetic below is my scratch calculator (python3 -I, no files written, nothing in either repo touched); re-derive in Rust before anyone cites it.
VERIFIED: the worked numbers reproduce: C(38,<=4)=82,993; (n,m,l)=(131,4,33): N_p=394, N_s=1180, C(394,<=4)=9.99e8, C(1180,<=4)=8.07e10, block/attempt 0.616, G=212.6; degree-5 block/attempt 145.1, G=0.903; toy (11,4,4): rho=57.7, G=2.10. With l from the correct yield rule, equal-degree G (pure column count, D=4, n=131) is 22.7, 108, 207, 298, 376, 441, 499, 600, 825 at m=2,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,20, i.e. >1 at every m including m=2. UNPROVED/likely false (c) selector-lifting lemma. Substituting s=e_k, s0=e_j is a ring homomorphism, so D_u >= max_k D_c(k) rigorously. The converse lift costs one degree per selector multiplication, and the symmetric last link is CUBIC (X_R linear in s0) where each component's is QUADRATIC (target constant; examples/descent_degree_cost.rs:85-87; src/cryptanalysis/polynomial_reuse.rs header). Naive lift therefore needs the degree-2 relations s0_j*s0_j' times a degree-2 multiplier: D_c+2, not D_c+1. The {D_c, D_c+1} dichotomy omits D_c+2, where pure G = 8e-4..4.5e-3 (m=2..20).
(d) 'G <= 1 at every m' is off by a hair even at +1: G(+1, D_c=4) = 0.18, 0.59, 0.88, 1.04, 1.11, 1.12, 1.12, 1.08, 1.01, 0.88, 0.76 at m=2,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,12,16,20 (max 1.12 before pen; the idea's 'minimum ~150' comes from the mistyped l). Immaterial once pen >= ~2, but misstated.
(e) Toy cells cannot reach the promotion branch: pure equal-degree G at D=3/4/5 = (3,5,1) 0.39/0.09/0.02; (3,7,1) 0.57/0.12/0.02; (3,7,2) 1.00/0.25/0.06; (4,5,1) 0.83/0.25/0.07, so block/attempt = rho/n >= 7 everywhere: 'D_u = D_c with block/attempt < 1' cannot fire at n <= 7.
(f) Three of four cells have l=1: V = span(1) = F_2 is sigma-stable, sigma^k V = V, the n components coincide and D_u = D_c trivially - a spurious route to 'D_u = D_c'.
(g) Cap: the only non-degenerate cell is (3,7,2); XL D_c ~ 5 there (research/factor_base_arity_review_20261024/README.md table m=3,l=2: XL 5), so D_u >= 5 and the quotient has 275,051 columns (30,436 at D=4) against the stated ~40k cap.
(h) 'Validate Burnside against on-disk counts' fails by construction: C(61,<=3)=37,882 all monomials vs 34,606 columns on disk at n=11 (9.5% over; the pure-c correction is only C(6,<=3)=42).
(i) Baseline: equal-degree batching already helps WITHOUT equivariance: gauge-fixed union (s0=e_0, N=1049) has C(1049,<=4)=5.04e10 vs n*C(394,<=4)=1.31e11 (0.38x); the quotient's extra factor is n/(N_s/N_gf)^D = 82. Both reverse if degree rises by one (gauge-fixed union at D+1 is 80x worse than n separate attempts).
END-TO-END (re-run of the cost_d4.py / descent_degree_cost.rs model, derived, units unconverted column touches): best case D_u = D_c with the same w on both arms lowers log2 total by 3.0 bits (m=4, w=1, pen=1), 8.5 (m=4, w=2), and by 0.25 / 2.2 at pen=80; gap to rho (2^60.81) stays +7.4 (w=1) / +30.9 (w=2) at m=4 (baseline +7.6 / +33.1). Baseline at w=2.2 is +35..+39 bits for every m=4..20 (D=4 held flat, unmeasured at m>=5). Frobenius already gives compact-orbit IC an n on relations against sqrt(2n) for rho (LEAD-ICB-frobenius-orbit-factor-base); the quotient does not change that ratio.

verdicts.title: Shared-prefix echelon reuse across targets and conjugates: equivariance used only to re-gauge
verdicts.math_check: WRONG, decisive. The premise 'R-independent fraction of Macaulay rows = (m-2)/(m-1)' counts equations, not rows. The final link is quadratic (target constant; src/cryptanalysis/polynomial_reuse.rs header 'D + sum_k r_k C_k'; examples/descent_degree_cost.rs:85-87 chain_degrees = (m-2)n cubics + n quadratics). At Macaulay degree D the cubic prefix takes multipliers of degree <= D-3 and the quadratic link <= D-2, so the shared share is s = (m-2)C(N,<=D-3) / [(m-2)C(N,<=D-3) + C(N,<=D-2)] ~ (D-1)(m-2)/N, and the best possible gain is 1/(1-s). Computed (mine): n=131, yield-rule l: m=3 (N=257) 1.008/1.012/1.016 at D=4/5/6; m=4 (N=390) 1.010/1.015/1.021; m=8 1.013/1.020/1.026; m=20 (N=2538) 1.014/1.021/1.028 - against the idea's 2, 3, 7, 19. Toy cells: (11,4,4) D=3..6: 1.051/1.105/1.162/1.221; (9,4,3) D=4: 1.133; (6,4,2) D=3..6: 1.095/1.199/1.312/1.436; (9,3,3) D=4: 1.110; (13,3,4) D=4: 1.080. s scales like 1/N ~ 1/n, so 'independent of n and l' is false and toy-scale gains are artefacts that vanish at n=131. m=2 giving exactly 1.0 is correct. At m=4 the idea's own kill line (A/B < 1.15) is already met at D<=4 on (11,4,4) (1.105), and its 'flat in m' falsifier would fire. Caveat (unmeasured): rows are XL rows of the original equations; if the degree-3 first-fall relations come from the prefix alone, the shared share of fall-derived rows could be larger.
verdicts.fatal_flaw: [WRONG] Row-share premise off by 30-1000x at n=131; the claimed m-1 scaling comes from counting equations while the target-dependent equation has far more multipliers. Also not Frobenius content and not new: IDEA-20260926-9c5694 (T4) states 'any elimination work shareable across the n conjugates is shareable across any n targets'; the target-independent prefix already exists as DecompositionTemplate.prefix (polynomial_reuse.rs:16-31); LEAD-ICB-multi-target-and-portfolio (closed_obstructed: amortisation only helps the online part and batch rho obeys the same multi-instance bound); KR-IC-f3da82 / EV-CERTBIN-6c3e0a (trace replay failed at n=17); IDEA-20260923-5d0b8e predicts replay retention ~2^-K. verdicts.title: Probe-prefix asymmetry in the pair-table oracle (cap the m=3 probe loop at rho*B; nested-probe oracle for m=4..8)
verdicts.math_check:
Reviewed read-only at crypto HEAD ba0384d9a and crypto-autoresearcher HEAD 6a69b2d02. Nothing was edited or rerun.

THE IDEA'S ARITHMETIC IS CORRECT UNDER ITS OWN MODEL. I recomputed the Poisson first-hit model with N sets, 3N uniformly placed probe positions, cost = min(first hit, rho*B), yield = 1-exp(-nu(1-(1-rho)^3)). Gain g over the full loop: nu=0.06..0.3 gives 2.5-2.9 at rho=0.1; nu=1 gives 2.13 (idea: 2.1-2.3); nu=3 gives 1.43 at rho=0.1 and 1.52 at rho=0.03 (idea says 1.6, slightly high); nu=10 gives 1.02; nu=30 gives 1.00. Worked n=13 toy: t_13=181, |E|=8012=4*2003 and 0.78B=28 probes are right. But B=36 is not a union of signed Frobenius orbits (2n=26), so it is not a valid mitm-frobenius base; B=26 gives nu=0.32 and B=52 gives nu=2.76.

THE DECISIVE CALCULATION IS THE BASELINE, NOT g. (a) Take one probe digit P_0 (rho*B=1). Probing R-P_0 against the pair table is the m=2 oracle applied to the fresh target R-P_0. Per relation that costs 2|E|/B^2 lookups plus one target step, which is the idea's own limit B/(3nu). (b) At nu>>1 the full m=3 loop returns after about B/(3nu) probes, which equals the m=2 oracle per relation. At nu<<1 the full loop is 3x worse than m=2. So g is a gain over a redundant loop and is <=1 against the m=2 oracle on the same table. The idea's own 'law check' (cost 2|E|/B^2 flat in m) says the same. (c) The m=4..8 'C(m,2) limit' (6, 15, 28) is relative to a sorted full-F nested loop that no code in the repo runs. The correct baseline at any m is the m=2 oracle on a shifted target. The table-size x probes law is the generic-group bound already priced in LEAD-ICB-generic-table-oracle (Shoup T>=sqrt(r/|Aut|), CGK S*T^2>~r/|Aut|). The idea's cheapest_test names the m=2 'subtract' arm (no table, B probes) as reference, which is the wrong arm.

PRODUCTION SIZING. For Table A rows (docs/ic/LEADERBOARD.md lines 79-84), nu=C(|F|,3)/r is 0.233 (n47: |F|=5264, r=106781081677), 0.235 (n57), 0.086 (n41), 0.169 (n53), 0.185 (n59), 0.061 (n61). That is exactly the nu<=0.3 gain regime. The manifest window is 164/5264=0.031, where the idea's model gives g=2.7-2.9.

m DEPENDENCE: the argument is flat in m (idea's own law check). Nothing here depends on the owner's m=2/3 concern.

CORRECT PARTS. S3(a,b,c)=a^2b^2+a^2c^2+b^2c^2+abc+1 (curve constant 1). With e1=b+c, e2=bc, S3=e2^2+a*e2+a^2*e1^2+1 in characteristic 2. Check: a^2(b+c)^2=a^2b^2+a^2c^2, e2^2=b^2c^2, a*e2=abc. The map is F_2-linear in the bits of (e1,e2). For generic V, L(l)=l(l+3)/2 unknowns: l=3->9, 4->14, 5->20, 6->27, 13->104, 14->119, 15->135>131. verdicts.title: Representation-multiplicity (clumping) law for the (Z/2)^m x S_m group at m = 2..8: exact census, compound-Poisson hit rate, Fano factor 2^(m-1), and triviality after cofactor projection
verdicts.math_check:
Re-derived and correct: x(P+T)=sqrt(b)/x(P) (chord through T=(0,sqrt b) gives x3=y_T/x1), so 1/x for b=1 and u=1/(x+1) -> u+1. #E(F_2)=4 with (1,0) of order 4 and 2(1,0)=(0,1)=T. Lucas V_13=181, #E(K0/F_{2^13})=8012=4*2003 with 2003 prime; n=7: 116=4*29. The free (Z/2)^{m-1} action on ordered point tuples, E[orbits]=lambda/2^{m-1}, Fano 2^{m-1}, and the T-class MITM per-hit tax 2^{m/2-1} (1, 1.41, 2, 2.83, 4, 8 for m=2,3,4,5,6,8) all check out, as do the 0.587/0.223/0.200 numbers for n=31, m=3.
But:
(i) 'n_rep(R)=0 mod 2^{m-1} for EVERY R, exact, deterministic' is false at the multiset level. If P and P+T are both in the T-closed base, the multiset {P,P+T} is fixed by the even translation (1,1) (it swaps the two points), so for m=2 and R=2P+T the count has an odd contribution. A census over all R, as proposed, contains N such R, so falsifier (i) fires deterministically on a 'clean' T-closed base. The correct statement holds for ordered point tuples, or after excluding stabilised tuples.
(ii) Fano/hit-rate calibration ignores the Z/4 component. E ~ Z/4 x Z/r, and T-closure forces p_a=p_{a+2} for the base's Z/4-component histogram. A non-uniform histogram makes the whole-group decomposable fraction a mixture of Poissons, not 1-exp(-lambda-bar/2^{m-1}). This is not controlled, so the 3-sigma test (iii) can fail for a benign reason.
(iii) The law is already confirmed. Ratio lambda_u/lambda_x = ln(1-h_u)/ln(1-h_x) against (N_u/N_x)^m/2^{m-1}: m=2: 0.412 vs 0.426 (n17), 0.443 vs 0.457 (n23a), 0.617 vs 0.548 (n23b) [research/koblitz_symmetrised_e2e_20260927/RESULTS.md, table]; m=3, n=31: 0.395 vs 0.381 [research/isogeny_fibers_20261010/parts/p7b_a1_results.md:17-42, which states 'representations over a +T-closed base come in 2^{m-1} copies']. It is a theorem plus four confirming cells; the only new content is m>=4, where no oracle exists.
(iv) Ill-posed. [4] sends P and P+T to the same element, so the projected image of an N-point T-closed base has N/2 elements, while the x-frame base projects to N. At matched projected size both are plain subsets of Z/r with the same Poisson law, so 'difference <2%' is a tautology (it can fail only by size mismatch). It is the already-implemented 'projected=1' fold of A1.
(v) The consequence check compares unlike quantities. The cited 'measured 1.18-1.28 at m=3 (n=31)' is S/S_x=1.18 for m=3 (projected, whole pipeline) and 1.28 for m=2 (unprojected, mitm-u/mitm-x); the formula predicts 1.41 (m=3) and 1.00 (m=2). The primary metric (GAE per independent relation) measured 2.95x worse at m=3 (p7b). No T-class-reduced MITM exists; mitm-u lists all 2,357 points (1.15x cost per trial).
(vi) After [4] T vanishes and r is prime, so the production group has no T; rho has no analogue, so the calibration cannot move the gap. The program's literature group is larger: GG14 section 3.3 uses (Z/4)^{m-1} x| S_m for E(F_2)=Z/4 (orbit 4^{m-1} m!), which is not addressed. The claim that FGHR does not account for the hit-rate tax is unverified; GG14 lines ~640-700 state the orbit size but I did not find the yield statement.
verdicts.fatal_flaw: UNSUPPORTED/redundant and partly ill-posed, but not wrong in its core. (a) It restates a law already derived and measured (p7b 7.A1-R reading 2; e2e table), so the new content is m>=4 with no consumer. (b) Falsifier (i) fires by construction and (iv) is a tautology. (c) The consequence is 'matched' to non-comparable measurements. (d) It is an accounting statement, not an improvement. Taken at face value it supports the opposite of the owner's 'the group grows with m, so the gain grows' intuition for T-closed bases: the tax grows as 2^{m-1} (19 bits at m=20) against a constant 2x column saving, and A1 already shows the projected x-frame / trace-zero base is 1.65x cheaper in S at equal columns (m=3). LEAD-STR-torsion-module-leak records the rational-torsion lever as 'a constant, and absent at prime order'.
verdicts.cheapest_falsification: No solver. For (i), take the committed n=17 T-closed base (409 points, research/koblitz_symmetrised_e2e_20260927), pick P with P and P+T in the base, set R=2P+T, and brute-force n_rep(R) at m=2; an odd count falsifies (i) as stated. For (ii)/(iii) at m=3,4,5, an exact bitset-sumset census on K0/F_{2^13} (#E=8012) takes seconds. Pre-register a mixture-corrected prediction using the base's Z/4-component histogram, and compare against the x-frame control at matched projected size.
verdicts.strongest_version: Theorem: for the (Z/2)^{m-1} translation action on ordered point tuples over a T-closed negation-closed base, n_rep is a multiple of 2^{m-1}; at the multiset level n_rep = 2^{m-1}K + O(stabilised tuples), with K ~ Poisson(lambda_a/2^{m-1}) computed per Z/4 coset a, and Fano = 2^{m-1}(1+O(m^2/N)). Verify at m=4,5 on n=13 and cite m=2,3 as already confirmed. Quote the T-class MITM break-even 2^{m/2-1} only if such an oracle is built. Replace (iv) by a unit test of the projected=1 fold at matched projected size. Label it accounting and calibration. State the consequence honestly: at m>=4 a T-closed base is dominated by projected x-frame or trace-zero bases, and there is no S reduction and no change in the gap to rho.

(5) Baseline mismatch (AGENTS.md section 15). It compares against crate gf2_elim on an XL Macaulay matrix at D=l+2. verdicts.title: The one place Frobenius is a genuine stabiliser: closed sums with R in E(F_2) on a sigma-stable base, yield tax n versus equivariant gain n^(omega-1)/c_ext
verdicts.math_check:
(1) Target class. G meet E(F_2) = {O} (|E(F_2)|=4 is coprime to r), so 'R in E(F_2)' is the target-free closed sum sum P_i = O. That is the free-relation object (LEAD-ICB-free-relations-self-collision: 49 independent rows out of 588 at n61/K600, a constant 0.957-0.960x of the complete solve). The arity review already names 'V stable and x_R in F_2' as the only Frobenius-stable case and dismisses it for random targets (research/factor_base_arity_review_20261024/README.md:301).
(2) Orbit size convention. Negation fixes x-tuples, so orbits of sigma on x-tuples have size n (n prime; only tuples in F_2^m are fixed), not 2n. Rows per solution is then 1/n=0.0323, not 1/(2n)=0.0161. Claim (2)'s +-25% tolerance excludes the other convention, so the claim is falsified or confirmed by convention alone.
(3) The predicted band does not follow from the cost model. With gain n^{omega-1}/c_ext at n=31, c_ext=6: 5.2 (omega=2), 20.4 (omega=2.4), 160 (omega=3). Tax 2n=62 gives net cost-per-row ratio 12.0, 3.0, 0.39; tax n gives 6.0, 1.5, 0.19. The stated band [0.8,3] matches none of these, and the proposal's own 'math' paragraph says 3-12x worse. The dense kernels actually used here are cubic with word packing (omega~3), where the same formulas give a GAIN (0.19-0.39). The sign of the 'expected null' is exponent-dependent, so it is not a pre-registered null. Using measured kernel gains instead of the model (equivariant vs gf2_elim on the symmetric matrix: 2.15x at n=11, 3.15x at n=13; step-level I/C 0.40-1.65x at n=7-23; research/ic_improve_20261014/02-equivariant-oracle/README.md sections 3-4) against the model's ~20-28x at n=11-13 gives net ~n/3, about a 10x loss at n=31.
(4) The tax is applied asymmetrically. An equivariant solve returns the whole quotient variety; so does a plain F4/FGLM solve of the same closed system; both give Z/n independent orbit-basis rows. The tax exists only against an unfolded baseline (each orbit member a separate column), which is not the production baseline, or against a one-solution-per-call oracle whose duplicates are negligible while rows needed << #orbits. 'k conjugates of a relation are one row in the orbit basis' is already C4 of the closed lead.
(5) Scope. Stable V at n=83 and 131 has dimensions {0,1,n-1,n} only, so no m=83 evidence (AGENTS.md section 8a) or ECC2K-130 evidence is possible. n=31 (ord 5, split cyclotomic block), n=23 (ord 11) and n=15 (composite) are structurally unlike 83/131.
(6) Closed sums need >=|F| solutions, N^{m-1}>=m!*#E: at n=31, dim 10, N~1,024 and ~7.8k expected solutions at m=4. Sorting or meet-in-the-middle finds them in ~N^{m/2} lookups, so the table oracle (not Macaulay elimination) is the baseline. Nothing here has an S column; the unit is XORs, a stage diagnostic.
verdicts.fatal_flaw: UNSUPPORTED / internally inconsistent, not wrong about the fixed point. (a) The pre-registered band [0.8,3] is not derived from the stated model, and the sign flips with omega; the falsifier ('net <=0.8 means Frobenius pays') is met under omega=3 by the model alone. (b) The 'tax' double-counts the orbit multiplicity against a baseline that does not exist in production. (c) The orbit-size convention is off by 2. (d) The experiment says nothing about C3 (single-instance orbit encodings, a different object) or about C5 as measured (kernel gain at m=2). (e) It cannot reach the m=83 gate. (f) It re-labels the known free-relation harvest and C4, so the gap to rho is unchanged.
verdicts.cheapest_falsification: Before any run, write the cost-per-independent-orbit-basis-relation formula with both arms priced on the SAME closed system, orbit-folded columns, and the tax removed from the plain arm. Then measure one thing: the kernel ratio at n=31 (d=5, F_32 tables) on one symmetric closed Macaulay matrix (rank identity + counted XORs vs gf2_elim and M4RI). The model predicts >=20x; the calibration at n=11,13 says ~1/10 of the model. If the ratio is <5x the net is a loss under any convention and the card closes; if >=20x the 'null' prediction is wrong.
verdicts.strongest_version: Narrow to a kernel calibration on closed sigma-stable systems: equivariant blocks vs M4RI/gf2_elim at n=15,23,31 (stable V, R=O, m=3,4), reporting rows per solution (1/n at x-level) and block-cost ratio. Compare cost per independent orbit-basis relation with the sorting-based free-relation harvest in counted ops at 0/0.1/1 GAE per unpriced native op (AGENTS.md section 5a, every arm including rho). Label it a stage diagnostic and engineering. Make no ECC2K-130 or m=83 transfer claim. Predict that it does not move any Table A-C row.
